Analysis.object: The TCM was partially supported in the context of eating disorders in the bodybuilders and runners. Both types of motivations for sport were direct or indirect risk factors for the development of deviant behaviors, but CM seemed to indicate greater risk than autonomous motivation for the development of eating disorders.

First, our sample was composed of young male with different numbers of years of practice, hours of practice per week, and types of practices (i.e., noncompetitors, future competitors, competitors), which might infuenced their motivation and engagement. Second, the runners were older than the bodybuilders, and younger people are more at risk of developing eating disorders than older people. Third, the data were collected using a self-report survey and might have been influenced by social desirability. Fourth, no model/theory on body image in male was used, although body dissatisfaction was clearly present, and drive for muscularity was not considered. Fifth, our study was correlational. Sixth, it would be useful to determine a cutoff for eating disorders in male athletes because the EAT is not adapted to measure eating disorders in male athletes desiring to gain muscle mass. Finally, the motivational mechanisms explaining the development of eating disorders in male bodybuilders and runners who desire to gain muscle mass/lean body mass need to be further investigated in terms of motivational profiles.

Include the level of competition in the analyses. Another model that also takes into account sociocognitive variables, such as the Health Action Process Approach might be applied in future research. Future studies could also specifically measure body satisfaction and analyze the link between this variable, behaviors to gain muscle mass/lean body mass, and the development of eating disorders.  It would be interesting to conduct a longitudinal study to more closely examine causality in the relationships. An intraindividual approach would be more useful than an interindividual approach. 
It appears necessary to limit the deleterious effects of controlled motivation. This might be accomplished by identifying the motivational orientations of athletes and promoting the development of coaching styles and climates that support autonomy and basic needs. Given the paradoxical role of autonomous motivation observed in the present study, it also appears necessary to encourage athletes to build reasoned and healthy sports parctices, limiting muscle mass gain at all costs.

Population.object: Minimum of 16 years; minimum of 3 hours of physical training per week; and minimum of 3 years of bodybuilding or running.
